section_summary: This section documents increasingly restrictive conditions governing foreign travel to and from wartime Japan, including transportation shortages, visa and admission rules, compulsory exit permits, and disputes over consular visa fees. It also contains numerous cross-reference sheets concerning refugees and a substantial case file on efforts by Senator William H. King and the State Department to secure visas, travel funds, and information for Aron Tigner and his family. The final document begins correspondence about the Tigner case but continues beyond page 80.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 4658: Unfavorable travel conditions in Japan
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Reports severe rail, steamship, hotel, and supply difficulties affecting travelers in Japan.
subfiles.summary: The Embassy warns that wartime traffic has made railway and steamship accommodations extremely difficult to obtain, sometimes immobilizing travelers for weeks. Tokyo also has a serious hotel-room shortage, while tightening controls over food, coal, and gasoline make future conditions uncertain.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference: Extension of Japanese visas for aliens in Russia
subfiles.from: William H. King, United States Senate
subfiles.about: Points to a letter concerning State Department intercession for extensions of Japanese visas held by aliens in Russia.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Senator King's request for help extending Japanese visas for aliens in Russia, filed under Aron D. Tigner.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 55: Assurance of admission of aliens into Japan
subfiles.from: W. Garland Richardson, American Consulate General, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Explains that Japanese authorities will not guarantee in advance that foreign visa holders will be admitted to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Richardson reports that Japanese officials refuse written or oral assurances of admission for aliens, particularly first-time visitors, even when Japanese consular visas have been issued. The Foreign Office will guarantee only that Japanese passport holders may return to Japan, prompting a suggestion that American consuls be alerted.

subfiles.title: Letter on Yokohama Water Police admission policy
subfiles.from: Richard F. Boyce, American Consul, Yokohama
subfiles.to: W. Garland Richardson, American Vice Consul, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Transmits findings concerning Isaacs A. Levy and the admission of aliens holding Japanese visas.
subfiles.summary: Boyce says Yokohama Water Police usually admit visa holders but may exclude for lack of funds, disease or dangerous ideas, will not guarantee Levy's admission, and prefectures set length of stay.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Isaacs A. Levy and Japanese entry policy
subfiles.from: Jule L. Goetzmann, American Vice Consul
subfiles.about: Records a discussion with Japanese police officials about Levy's visa and the rules for admitting foreigners.
subfiles.summary: Japanese officials describe transit and entry visas, including special limitations sometimes imposed on stateless persons and White Russians. They emphasize that prefectural authorities may exclude even consular visa holders and refuse to guarantee Levy's or any other foreigner's admission before arrival.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference: Japanese transit visas issued at Kaunas
subfiles.from: Laurence A. Steinhardt, U.S. Embassy in the Soviet Union
subfiles.about: Points to a telegram about approximately 2,000 Japanese transit visas issued in Kaunas for travel toward Dutch possessions in the Americas.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to a telegram: on Dutch assurances, about 2,000 Japanese transit visas were issued at Kaunas.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference: Japanese Embassy cooperation on transit visas
subfiles.from: Laurence A. Steinhardt, U.S. Embassy in the Soviet Union
subfiles.about: Points to a telegram stating that Japanese transit visas would be issued only upon applicants' appearance.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: the Japanese Embassy would cooperate on refugee transit cases but required applicants to appear personally.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference: Frances M. Black visa-fee refund
subfiles.about: Points to a despatch requesting a refund of the Japanese visa fee paid by Frances M. Black.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to a despatch asking whether the Japanese visa fee collected from teacher Frances Black of Sendai should be refunded.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference: Suspension of Japanese transit visas at Sofia
subfiles.about: Points to a telegram reporting orders that the Japanese Legation at Sofia issue no more transit visas to America.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: the Japanese Legation in Sofia reportedly was told to stop issuing transit visas for travel to America.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference: Transit certificates restricted to Moscow
subfiles.about: Points to a telegram reporting that Japanese transit certificates would be issued only at Moscow.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: restricting Japanese transit certificates to Moscow was expected to curtail refugee movement through Japan to the United States.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference: No United States assurances for rabbis and students
subfiles.about: Points to a telegram declining intervention for rabbis and students then in Vladivostok.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: the Department would not approach Japanese authorities for a group of rabbis and students or imply U.S. visas would follow.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference: Refugee travel without Portuguese or Japanese transit visas
subfiles.about: Points to a communication asking whether refugee visas should be granted when onward travel could not be assured.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: Portuguese and Japanese authorities issued no transit visas for refugees; asks whether other visas should be granted or suspended.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference: Japanese visa difficulty of Dr. John D. Maple
subfiles.about: Points to a memorandum concerning Dr. John D. Maple's difficulty obtaining a Japanese visa.
subfiles.summary: Maple was an assistant entomologist with the Department of Agriculture. His Japanese visa problem was cross-filed under departmental personnel correspondence.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference: Immigration regulations and refugees in Japan
subfiles.about: Points to a voluntary report on refugees arriving in Japan with expiring United States immigration visas.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to a report on refugees whose U.S. quota visas lapsed after four months; most refugees in Japan also had authorization to reside elsewhere.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 1048: Restrictions on foreigners at Kobe
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, Tokyo, forwarding a message from Warner at Kobe
subfiles.about: Reports specific restrictions imposed on foreign travel and access in Kobe and Osaka.
subfiles.summary: Telegram No. 1048: Joseph Sutton was refused passage to Nagasaki, foreigners were barred from Kobe wharves, British Consul MacDermot was denied a railway ticket, and foreign chambers overlooking the harbor were asked to move.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference: Japanese retaliatory visa policy
subfiles.about: Points to a despatch about Japanese retaliation for British treatment of Japanese visa applicants.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to a despatch describing a Japanese visa policy as retaliation for British handling of Japanese applicants; no further details survive.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference: Interference with visas for travel through Japan
subfiles.about: Points to a communication about impediments to visas for nongovernmental travelers proceeding through Japan to the United States.
subfiles.summary: Damaged cross-reference: further visas were not being issued to some non-officials, who may need to defer travel until they obtain a Japanese visa.

subfiles.title: Division memorandum on revised Japanese alien regulations
subfiles.about: Calls attention to Tokyo despatch No. 5801 and Japan's new requirement that aliens obtain permission to leave.
subfiles.summary: Memorandum on Japan's revised alien regulations: all aliens must now obtain official permission before leaving Japan.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 5801: Revision of Japanese regulations governing aliens
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Transmits and analyzes Japan's revised regulations on alien visas, entry, residence, and departure.
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 5801: revised rules cut normal visa validity to six months, generally allow one entry, and require a prefectural permit before departure; consular officers refer more cases to Tokyo.

subfiles.title: Translation of Ordinance No. 23, Ministry of Home Affairs
subfiles.about: Sets out the formal amendments governing alien entry, sojourn, and departure from Japan.
subfiles.summary: The ordinance restricts visa validity and use, permits conditional special entry, and requires resident aliens to apply for departure permits three days in advance. Prefectural governors may dictate departure details, alter conditions upon application, and penalize unauthorized departure. Transitional rules govern previously issued visas and aliens leaving immediately after promulgation.

subfiles.title: File divider for individual-name cases
subfiles.about: Directs researchers to the old file for individual-name cases dated before July 1, 1940.
subfiles.summary: File divider for individual-name cases under 894.111; pre-July 1940 cases are in the old file.

subfiles.title: Despatch on Frances Marion Black's Japanese visa fee
subfiles.from: Richard F. Boyce, American Consul, Yokohama
subfiles.about: Requests a determination and possible refund of the ten-dollar Japanese visa fee paid by Frances Marion Black.
subfiles.summary: Boyce encloses Frances Black's receipt for a ten-dollar Seattle visa fee for teaching at Miyagi Girls' School, asking for a refund if improper.

subfiles.title: Japanese Consulate receipt issued to Frances Marion Black
subfiles.about: Records Black's payment of a ten-dollar entrance-visa fee.
subfiles.summary: Bilingual Japanese Consulate receipt for ten dollars from Frances Marion Black for an entrance visa.

subfiles.title: Department decision denying Frances Black's refund request
subfiles.from: Breckinridge Long for the Secretary of State
subfiles.to: Richard F. Boyce, American Consul, Yokohama
subfiles.about: Concludes that Frances Black was not a temporary visitor eligible for a fee waiver.
subfiles.summary: The Department reviews Black's status as a missionary teacher residing in Japan for an indefinite period. Because the 1926 Visa Waiver Agreement applied to Americans temporarily visiting for business or pleasure, it found no appropriate basis for requesting a refund.

subfiles.title: Passport Division memorandum on the Black refund case
subfiles.about: Records internal agreement that Frances Black lacked temporary-visitor status.
subfiles.summary: Passport Division memorandum: with Coulter of Visa Division, concluded Black could not claim the 1926 waiver without showing her stay was temporary.

subfiles.title: Far Eastern Affairs memorandum on Ruth Leitzel's visa
subfiles.about: Summarizes the finding that refusal of Ruth Leitzel's transit visa resulted from a decoding error rather than discrimination.
subfiles.summary: Memorandum on Ruth Leitzel's visa: the Peiping consulate misread instructions as requiring referral of every application to Tokyo; two-week transit visas still issue locally, and the Embassy regretted the error.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 3064: Refusal of Japanese visa to Ruth R. Leitzel
subfiles.from: Robert L. Smyth, American Embassy, Peiping
subfiles.about: Explains the mistaken refusal of a Japanese transit visa to American citizen Ruth R. Leitzel.
subfiles.summary: Second Secretary Ringwalt learned that the Japanese consular passport officer had incorrectly decoded instructions requiring visitor-visa applications to be referred to Tokyo. Two-week transit visas remained issuable without referral, and the Embassy found no evidence of discrimination against American nationals.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 4482: Refund of Albert H. Terry's visa fee
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Reports that Japan refunded the ten-dollar visa fee charged to Albert H. Terry.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ministry of Foreign Affairs refunded ¥42.66, equivalent to the disputed ten-dollar fee. The money was forwarded to Terry, and his receipt was enclosed with the despatch.

subfiles.title: Albert H. Terry's receipt for refunded visa fee
subfiles.about: Acknowledges receipt of ¥42.66 as reimbursement for the Japanese visa fee collected in San Francisco.
subfiles.summary: Albert Terry confirms receiving, through the American Consulate, a refund of the ten dollars paid in San Francisco.

subfiles.title: Department letter acknowledging the Albert Terry fee case
subfiles.from: George S. Messersmith for the Secretary of State
subfiles.to: Richard F. Boyce, American Consul, Yokohama
subfiles.about: Advises that the Department was asking the Tokyo Embassy to obtain a refund for Terry.
subfiles.summary: Department says the ten-dollar San Francisco fee in Albert Terry's case appears contrary to the visa-waiver agreement and promises further word.

subfiles.title: Instruction No. 1799 on Albert Terry's visa fee
subfiles.to: Eugene H. Dooman, Chargé d'Affaires ad interim, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Directs the Embassy to seek reimbursement of Terry's Japanese visa fee.
subfiles.summary: Instruction No. 1799 compares Albert Terry's fee case with Ernest Vest's and asks that the Foreign Office refund his ten dollars.

subfiles.title: Despatch reporting the visa fee charged to Albert Henry Terry
subfiles.from: Richard F. Boyce, American Consul, Yokohama
subfiles.about: Reports the Japanese Consulate General's collection of a ten-dollar visa fee from Albert Terry.
subfiles.summary: Terry paid for a visa to join the American President Lines staff in Yokohama after initially being quoted fifteen dollars. Boyce argues that comparable Japanese steamship employees received free American visas and asks whether Terry should seek a refund.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 711: Tigner not found at Lviv address
subfiles.about: Reports that a registered follow-up letter to Aron Tigner was returned because he could not be located.
subfiles.summary: Telegram No. 711: postal authorities say Tigner is not at his Lviv address nor registered there; Senator King had been advised.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 609: No information on Tigner's whereabouts
subfiles.about: Reports unsuccessful efforts to contact Aron Tigner and offers to report later developments.
subfiles.summary: Telegram No. 609: no reply to the Embassy's registered letter to Tigner; Steinhardt says the Foreign Office would not entertain inquiries on his whereabouts.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 55 requesting an immediate Tigner status report
subfiles.from: Sumner Welles, Acting Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Requests an immediate report on Aron Tigner for Senator King and other interested persons.
subfiles.summary: Telegram No. 55 asks Moscow for Tigner's present status, briefly, stating the cost.

subfiles.title: Accounts memorandum on refund of Tigner funds
subfiles.about: Records the disposition of money remaining from funds remitted in the Tigner case.
subfiles.summary: Damaged accounts memorandum: Tigner funds refunded to a Los Angeles bank on April 23, 1941.

subfiles.title: Special Division memorandum on Tigner's $500 deposit
subfiles.about: Reviews Senator King's request to recover money deposited for Aron Tigner and identifies expenses already deducted.
subfiles.summary: Embassy accounts showed that $500 had been held for Tigner, with small amounts used for an affidavit in lieu of a passport and an immigration visa, leaving approximately $487. Because the Department could not identify the original remitter, it asked Senator King to obtain instructions from Tigner's relatives concerning repayment.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 239 concerning reports of Tigner's imprisonment
subfiles.about: Asks whether Tigner's Philippine visa should be sent to Lviv after reports that he was imprisoned there.
subfiles.summary: Telegram No. 239: Mrs. Tigner reports her husband imprisoned for lacking a passport; Moscow asked about mailing the visa and his whereabouts and plans.

subfiles.title: Visa Division memorandum on Tigner's reported imprisonment
subfiles.about: Records Senator King's report that Aron Tigner was imprisoned in Lviv.
subfiles.summary: Visa Division memorandum: Mrs. Tigner reportedly wrote that her husband was held in Lviv; Coulter agreed to cable Moscow at King's expense.

subfiles.title: Senator King's payment of Tigner-case expenses
subfiles.from: William H. King, United States Senate
subfiles.about: Transmits Harold Cline's check covering Department expenses in the Aron Tigner matter.
subfiles.summary: Senator King encloses Harold Cline's check for $99.25 for State Department expenses in the Tigner case.

subfiles.title: High Commissioner's letter on unpaid Tigner telegram charges
subfiles.from: Woodbury Willoughby for the United States High Commissioner to the Philippines
subfiles.about: Discusses settlement of a $3.57 telegram expense incurred in the Tigner visa case.
subfiles.summary: High Commissioner's letter asking Resident Commissioner Elizalde, who intervened for Tigner, to contact the Department about unpaid telegram charges.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 1812: Tigner documents returned undelivered
subfiles.about: Reports that Tigner's affidavit and Philippine visa were returned and that he might have gone to Kraków.
subfiles.summary: Telegram No. 1812: documents mailed October 29 returned as Tigner left no forwarding address; he may have tried to reach Kraków, and Steinhardt suggests inquiry through Berlin.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 920 requesting verification of Tigner's receipt of visa
subfiles.about: Asks whether Tigner received his Philippine visa and requests that his funds remain available.
subfiles.summary: Telegram No. 920: relatives want confirmation of Tigner's location, welfare and receipt of the visa; the Embassy should keep money held for him.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 1712: Tigner mail returned
subfiles.about: Reports the return of Tigner's registered affidavit and Philippine visa.
subfiles.summary: Telegram No. 1712: documents mailed to Tigner October 29 returned marked that he had departed, address unknown.

subfiles.title: Visa Division memorandum requesting a report on Tigner
subfiles.about: Records Senator King's request for confirmation of Tigner's receipt of his visa and retention of his funds.
subfiles.summary: Visa Division memorandum: King asks the Department to cable Moscow on whether the Philippine visa was delivered and to keep holding Tigner's money.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 1612: No word from Tigner
subfiles.about: Reports that the Moscow Embassy had heard nothing from Tigner since mailing his documents.
subfiles.summary: Telegram No. 1612: the affidavit and Philippine visa, issued on applications signed March 29, 1940 in Lviv, were mailed October 29 with no acknowledgment.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 794 requesting news of Tigner
subfiles.about: Requests information on whether Tigner received his visa and was preparing to travel.
subfiles.summary: Telegram No. 794 asks Moscow for news on whether Tigner obtained the Philippine visa, stating the reply cost.

subfiles.title: Visa Division memorandum on fears for Tigner
subfiles.about: Records Senator King's request for a report and Mrs. Tigner's fear that her husband had been sent to Siberia.
subfiles.summary: Visa Division memorandum: King wants confirmation that Tigner got the visa; Mrs. Tigner fears he was sent to Siberia or an impostor took his visa.

subfiles.title: Letter confirming mailing of Tigner's documents
subfiles.from: Eliot B. Coulter, Acting Chief, Visa Division
subfiles.about: Confirms that Tigner's affidavit and Philippine visa were mailed to him in Lviv.
subfiles.summary: Coulter confirms to Senator King that Moscow mailed both documents to Tigner on October 29.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 1435: Tigner documents mailed
subfiles.about: Reports mailing an affidavit in lieu of passport and a Philippine visa to Aron Tigner.
subfiles.summary: Telegram No. 1435: documents were mailed to Tigner's Lviv address on October 29, answering the Department's status request.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 694 requesting current status of Tigner case
subfiles.about: Requests a report on Tigner's Philippine visa and any difficulties affecting the case.
subfiles.summary: Telegram No. 694 asks Moscow for the current Tigner status, whether he knows visa procedure, and any obstacles.

subfiles.title: Visa Division memorandum on Senator King's request
subfiles.about: Records Senator King's request for a telegraphic status report on Aaron Tigner.
subfiles.summary: Visa Division memorandum authorizing an inquiry after King asked the Moscow Embassy to report promptly on the visa case.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 669 authorizing Tigner's Philippine visa
subfiles.about: Notifies Moscow that the Philippine Government authorized issuance of a visa to Aron David Tigner.
subfiles.summary: The telegram communicates the Philippine Government's approval of Tigner's entry. It refers back to the Department's September 17 inquiry.

subfiles.title: Suspect-list check on Aaron Tigner
subfiles.about: Records that Aaron Tigner's name produced no match in State Department suspect records.
subfiles.summary: The Visa Division checked its card index and consulted Mr. Fletcher Warren. No adverse record concerning Tigner was found.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Philippine authorization for Tigner
subfiles.about: Records Senator King's report that Philippine authorities had approved Tigner's admission.
subfiles.summary: Memorandum: watch for the Philippine authorization, cable Moscow when it arrives, and inform Senator King.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 648 authorizing Tigner's entry into the Philippines
subfiles.about: Reports Philippine Commonwealth authorization for Aron David Tigner's entry.
subfiles.summary: Telegram No. 648: Tigner is to apply at the Moscow Embassy; Sayre asks the Department to cable so the visa can be issued, with cable charges guaranteed.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 554 requesting report on Tigner's visa application
subfiles.about: Requests a report on Tigner's visa application, welfare, whereabouts, and plans.
subfiles.summary: Telegram No. 554 gives Tigner's Lviv address and asks when his application might be acted on, with any information on his condition or journey.

subfiles.title: Visa Division memorandum on the separated Tigner family
subfiles.about: Records concern for Aron Tigner after his wife and daughter reached the United States.
subfiles.summary: Coulter explains the U.S. cannot intervene officially for non-citizen Tigner but can seek visa information from Moscow; $500 remains available, and Samuel Cline is Tigner's brother-in-law.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 339 announcing transfer of $500 for Tigner
subfiles.about: Notifies Moscow that $500 had been forwarded for Aron David Tigner and his family's journey.
subfiles.summary: Telegram No. 339: $500 transferred via the Bank for Foreign Trade for Tigner; the family is traveling from Soviet-occupied Poland to the U.S. through Japan.

subfiles.title: Record of Senator King's call about Tigner travel funds
subfiles.about: Requests notification to Moscow that $500 had been sent for the Tigner family's journey.
subfiles.summary: Record of Senator King's call: Aron Tigner, wife and two children are going from Soviet-occupied Poland to the U.S. via Japan; he asks the Moscow Embassy be told of the remittance and pays the telegram.

subfiles.title: Letter transmitting news of the Tigner family's departure from Moscow
subfiles.about: Transmits a Moscow telegram reporting the departure of Tigner's wife and sons.
subfiles.summary: Welles encloses the June 19 Embassy report on Zofia, Jerzy and Marek Tigner and suggests King relay it to Samuel and Harold Cline.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 704: Zofia Tigner and sons depart Moscow
subfiles.about: Reports that Zofia Tigner and her sons left Moscow after obtaining Japanese transit visas.
subfiles.summary: Telegram No. 704: Zofia Tigner and her sons left Moscow for Vladivostok and Tokyo, due about July 8; Aron is to follow when he gets a Soviet exit visa.

subfiles.title: Letter enclosing the June 13 Tigner telegram
subfiles.about: Transmits additional information and recommendations concerning the Tigner family's journey.
subfiles.summary: Department encloses the Moscow Embassy's June 13 telegram, inviting King to refer its suggestions to Samuel and Harold Cline.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 671: Tigner family needs $500 for travel
subfiles.about: Reports that Zofia Tigner and her sons had Soviet exit visas and urgently needed money for travel to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Telegram No. 671: the Tigner mother and sons left Lviv for Moscow with exit visas; interested persons should telegraph $500 for travel.

subfiles.title: Letter transmitting June 6 and June 9 telegrams on the Tigner case
subfiles.about: Begins a letter forwarding Embassy reports about assistance and travel arrangements for the Tigner family.
subfiles.summary: Letter fragment transmitting June 6 and 9 telegrams: the Moscow Embassy informally helped the Tigners since December; begins travel suggestions for Jack Collins. Continues beyond page 80.
